clue.text: Cleaning equipment was black, kept in store

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something kept in a store sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a hoard is a stockpile or store
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A housekeeper's cleaning gear used to be black and was kept in the storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a place to keep the equipment, but it is a stockpile; 'kept in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridged board once used for scrubbing laundry by hand is a piece of cleaning kit.

clue.text: Know-all's message covers the main chapter

indicators.note: one piece covering others wraps round them, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a wire is an old word for a telegram, a message
the main is a poetic term for the open sea

explanation.surface: A smart alec's text message gives an account of a nautical chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after the definition reads as 'is', joining it to the wordplay; 'covers' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a person who affects to know everything, a smart alec or know-all.

clue.text: Carol's about to catch vehicle up in curious event

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the singing goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to carol is to sing; the 's reads as 'is'
to nail someone is to catch them

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means this word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A carol singer is about to grab a vehicle while taking part in a strange contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the vehicle and 'about' wraps the carol round the rest. This is a quirky English village contest, one of the puzzle's curious events.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing garden molluscs is an eccentric competition, held each year at Congham in Norfolk, so it counts as a curious event.

clue.text: Curious event where trap set up: drunk 23s, catching a thousand fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means this word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: gob is slang for the mouth, a trap

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside, so the thousand goes within
drunk signals that these letters are reeling about in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 23-down made plural, signs up becoming the six letters of that word with S
K is short for a thousand, from kilo
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: At an odd gathering, someone drunk signs up for a fish-catching trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles the 23-down word with S, and 'catching' puts K inside to make SNORKEL. The contest is swimming through a Welsh peat bog.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming through a muddy peat-bog trench in snorkel and flippers, held yearly in Llanwrtyd Wells, Wales, is plainly a curious event.

clue.text: Thought expert Gore invested in anyway?

indicators.note: something invested in another is clothed by it, so it goes inside

parts.note: split as any + way, with way giving ST, the abbreviation for street
Al Gore, the former US vice-president, supplies his first name AL

explanation.surface: Would a thinking specialist have put Al Gore in charge anyway?
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'anyway' as 'any way' with ST (street) for the way; 'invested in' puts AL inside ANY, then ST follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychoanalyst, or analyst for short, is an expert in how people think.

clue.text: Disaster proving hard to remove from bleached dicky

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so these letters are knocked out of order
these words tell us to take a letter away from the word that follows

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A calamity where a stained shirt front can't be got clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove from' takes H out of BLEACHED, leaving BLEACED; 'dicky' rearranges that. A dicky is also a detachable shirt front.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden humiliating collapse or failure, a disaster.

clue.text: Dashed hopes reap the reward always at the end

indicators.note: always at the end tells us to take the last letter of every one of these words

explanation.surface: Disappointed hopes are always rewarded in the end, as the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed hopes' reads as one phrase, but 'Dashed' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed in the sense of rushed or hurried along, a past tense synonym of went fast.

clue.text: Amount of tea to serve, right? One scented it is

parts.note: a pot is an amount of tea, as in a pot for two
to pour is to serve a drink
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Here's a pot of tea to pour, right? It's a fragrant one.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices whose whole purpose is to give off a pleasant smell.

clue.text: Half and half seen as the end

parts.note: demi is a prefix meaning half, as in demigod

indicators.note: half here means only the first half of the word that follows is used

explanation.surface: Something split fifty-fifty is regarded as finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Demise means death or ending, so it stands for the end.

clue.text: A cool glacier has almost melted, as remains to be studied

indicators.note: melted means losing shape, so the letters run into a new order
almost means the word falls short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A cool glacier has nearly thawed, leaving ancient remains to dig up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims HAS to HA; 'melted' scrambles A, COOL, GLACIER and HA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaeological describes things such as buried ruins and artefacts that are of interest to scholars of the past.

clue.text: Refuse to admit noun is common language

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: slag is refuse left after smelting ore
N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: Declining to confess that a word is ordinary speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb (to decline) but is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, colloquial vocabulary, the language of everyday common speech.

clue.text: Here planes perhaps penetrate through craft? I'm unsure

indicators.note: through here means running inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: art is craft or skill
to bore is to drill into or penetrate
um is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Do aircraft fly through the clouds here? I'm not sure.
explanation.walkthrough: Planes are plane trees, not aircraft, and 'penetrate' looks like the container signal while 'through' is.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a collection of trees grown for study, where plane trees might well be found.

clue.text: Fixed penalty to spare

indicators.note: a fixed result has been rigged or rearranged, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: A fixed penalty fine that you have money left over to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed penalty' reads as a traffic fine; 'Fixed' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplenty means in abundance, so there is more than enough, some to spare.

clue.text: Word of realisation among birds in this together?

indicators.note: among means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: coots are black water birds
ah is the exclamation when the penny drops

explanation.surface: An exclamation of discovery among a flock of birds who are all in this together.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase with 'this' standing in for the answer: in cahoots means colluding.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is an idiom for conspiring or working jointly, being in a thing together.

clue.text: Children's character sees rugby forward Jack tackling cup holder

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union
pert means forward or cheeky

indicators.note: tackling means grabbing round, so this word holds another inside it

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, so jack gives TAR
Hebe was cupbearer to the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A rugby forward named Jack tackles the player holding the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackling' signals the container. The answer is a long-running British comic-strip bear in checked trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: This check-trousered little bear has starred in British children's comic strips and annuals since 1920.

clue.text: Rye (so much for Agatha Christie!), where policeman turned up on time in amazing fluke

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means this word reads from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman

indicators.note: in places the time letter inside the scrambled letters
amazing means astonishing or confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Christie mystery title where a copper turns up just in time thanks to an amazing stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazing' scrambles the fluke to KEFUL, and 'in' places the time letter inside. Agatha Christie wrote A Pocket Full of Rye.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's novel title A Pocket Full of Rye tells us how much rye there was: this much.

clue.text: Soldier nursing king in time before victorious day, showing distress

indicators.note: before signals that this part comes first and the day follows it
in places the soldier piece inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the king goes inside the soldier

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
R is short for rex, Latin for king
VE Day marks Victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: A soldier holding the king in the age before Victory Day, looking upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' and 'in' nest the pieces to give AGGRIE; 'before' sets it ahead of the day. 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve someone is to cause them distress or a sense of grievance.

clue.text: Maybe he'll recognise curious event

indicators.note: maybe suggests these letters are one possible arrangement among others

explanation.surface: Perhaps he will spot an odd happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the definition, as in the other theme answers; 'Maybe' does the scrambling. Cheese rolling is chasing a cheese down a Gloucestershire hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing a rolling wheel of Double Gloucester down Cooper's Hill is a famous eccentric contest, a curious event.

clue.text: More cross southern river to rest in old city

indicators.note: in places the river and resting pieces inside the old city

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
to lie is to rest

explanation.surface: Southern river flows in to rest in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' splits the ancient city's two letters around the river and rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Surlier is the comparative of surly, so it means more bad-tempered or grumpy.

clue.text: End of four months in the red, becoming flexible

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the month ending goes inside

parts.note: ruby is a deep red colour
September, October, November and December all end in the same three letters

explanation.surface: After a third of the year in debt, a business becomes adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' suggests debt, but red is the colour. 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rubbery is springy and bends easily, so it is flexible.

clue.text: See 2
So nipple areas are getting cold, with top discarded

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: top discarded means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: polar means freezing cold

explanation.surface: Nipples stiffen when it gets cold, after taking one's top off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with top discarded' drops P from POLAR, leaving OLAR. 'So' means in the manner of, making the definition adjectival.
explanation.definitionFit: Areolar is the adjective for the areola, the ring of skin around the nipple.

clue.text: Stomach infection precedes nightmare

indicators.note: precedes means this part comes before the next piece

parts.note: a bug is an infection
to stomach something is to bear it

explanation.surface: A gastric bug comes before a bad dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach infection' reads as one illness, but 'Stomach' is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of dread or annoyance, a nightmare in the loose sense.

clue.text: Sign up name in learning to be upstanding

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters read from the bottom, backwards
in places the name letter inside the learning word

parts.note: lore is knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: Register your name to be upright in your studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside LORE to make LORNE; 'to be upstanding' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up or register for a course or membership.

clue.text: Silly, wearing cooler hat

parts.note: in means wearing, as in in a suit
a fan cools you
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Looking foolish in a hat that keeps you cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tile' is old British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantile means childish, and so foolish or silly.

clue.text: Cut right into hole underground

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the letter is placed within

parts.note: a cave is a hollow underground

explanation.surface: Cutting the right way into an underground hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut, as meat or stone.

clue.text: Scavenger's trick

definitions.meaning: a seabird that scavenges for food, with 's as 'is' linking

explanation.surface: The scavenger's ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is a seabird known for scavenging, and to gull someone means to deceive or trick them.

clue.text: As the Queen's blood?

parts.note: aristocrats are said to have blue blood, so a royal's blood would be this colour

explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep bright blue colour, punning on the blue blood of royalty.
